title: HOTC — Quarterly Performance Report
exec_summary: 607 business calls responded to across the Jul–Sep quarter — an average of roughly 6.6 calls every day — with September the single busiest month at 223 calls.
The Safety Team intervened in 36 serious incidents over the quarter (13 Jul · 8 Aug · 15 Sep), de-escalating and physically separating parties on the ground.
168 aggressive-behaviour incidents managed and de-escalated (peaking at 65 in September) — yet only 5 injuries recorded across the entire quarter, and zero in both July and September.
15 arrests supported (including citizen's arrests) — offenders detained and handed to Police — across the three months.

Police-attended incidents held to 74 for the quarter, down from 151 in the same period of 2024 (−51%) and below the 77 recorded in the same period of 2025 — fewer situations escalating to Police despite a heavier aggression load.
302 vagrancy-related responses delivered — welfare checks, move-ons and safeguarding of vulnerable and intoxicated people — the largest single incident category of the quarter.
107 retail-theft incidents attended, with goods recovered and offenders detained for Police; theft volume rose month-on-month (33 → 36 → 38).
73 assistance requests fulfilled for city businesses and the public, climbing steadily through the quarter (18 → 22 → 33).
Public-drinking incidents reduced to 80 for the quarter, down from 94 in 2025 and 116 in 2024 — a sustained year-on-year reduction consistent with the Safety Team's visible deterrent presence.
39 intoxicated persons safeguarded and 13 medical events attended, including welfare and first-response support.
213 incidents published to the Auror crime-intelligence platform (60 Jul · 79 Aug · 74 Sep) — building prosecution-ready offender intelligence shared with Police and retailers.
September stood out as the peak-demand month, posting the quarter's highest calls (223), aggression (65), serious incidents (15) and assistance (33) — all absorbed without a single recorded injury.

sections.title: Safety Improvement — Police & Aggression
paras: Police-attended incidents were held to 74 across the quarter (23 Jul, 22 Aug, 29 Sep) — roughly half the 151 recorded in the same period of 2024 (a 51% reduction) and below the 77 logged in the same period of 2025 (the 2025 figure is itself understated, as July 2025 captured only three reporting weeks). The trend is clear: fewer situations are escalating to Police attendance, even as the team manages a heavier aggression load. The Safety Team continues to intervene early, de-escalate and physically separate parties before incidents reach that threshold.

Aggressive-behaviour incidents rose to 168 for the quarter (53 Jul, 50 Aug, 65 Sep), up from 124 in the same period of 2025, and the team intervened in 36 serious incidents (13 Jul, 8 Aug, 15 Sep), with September the most demanding month. Despite that volume, only five injuries were recorded across the whole quarter — none in July or September — and 15 offenders were detained and handed to Police. The low harm outcome relative to the weight of aggression handled reflects disciplined, hands-on intervention.

sections.title: Deterrence & Coverage
paras: Across the quarter the team responded to 607 business calls — an average of about 6.6 a day — maintaining a consistent, visible presence across the city centre through peak and late-economy hours. Call volume has eased from prior years (822 in the same period of 2024, 660 in 2025) while the share of serious and aggressive work the team absorbs has grown, consistent with a more settled day-to-day baseline backed by a stronger response when it is needed.

Deterrence shows most clearly in public drinking, which fell to 80 incidents for the quarter — down from 94 in 2025 and 116 in 2024, a sustained year-on-year reduction that tracks the team's uniformed, high-visibility presence. That presence continues to suppress low-level antisocial behaviour before it escalates into something requiring Police.

sections.title: Vagrancy Response & Community Safety
paras: Vagrancy was the single largest incident category of the quarter at 302 responses (120 Jul, 76 Aug, 106 Sep), spiking in July and again in September. These are handled as welfare-first encounters — checking on rough sleepers, moving people on from business entrances where needed, and safeguarding vulnerable and intoxicated individuals — balancing compassion with public amenity.

Alongside this, the team fulfilled 73 assistance requests (rising 18 → 22 → 33 across the quarter), safeguarded 39 intoxicated persons and attended 13 medical events, including welfare and first-response support. The steadily rising assistance trend into September reflects the team being increasingly relied on by businesses and the public as a trusted first point of contact.

sections.title: Retail Theft & Recovery
paras: The team attended 107 retail-theft incidents across the quarter, with volume climbing each month (33 Jul, 36 Aug, 38 Sep). With a visible presence on the shop floor, the Safety Team deters offending, intervenes in thefts in progress, recovers goods and detains offenders for Police where it is safe to do so.

The steady month-on-month rise underlines retail crime as a persistent pressure on city-centre businesses, and the team's visible presence and rapid response remain the frontline control — stopping thefts as they occur and returning recovered goods to retailers.

caveats: Figures are drawn from the Safety Team's daily patrol reports for July–September 2026 and have been independently data-verified.

The detailed incident categories — vagrancy, theft, serious incidents, arrests, intoxication and medical events — have been recorded since March 2026; year-on-year comparisons for these measures before that date are shown as 'n/a' rather than estimated.
Theft values quoted in the highlights are indicative figures provided by store staff at the time and have not been independently verified.

'Total Activity' is a combined count of all recorded actions other than business calls; as a single incident can involve more than one category, it is a measure of overall activity rather than a count of distinct incidents.
'Patrol routes' counts the patrol routes commenced as recorded in the daily reports.
Police figures are compared both against the same quarter in prior years (in the summary) and against the prior-year monthly average (in the year-on-year table); both show a clear downward trend.
